record.interface_detail: Windows client for device management, a Docker image for Linux, and a web console for mappings.
record.tooling: vendor client on Windows/Linux/Docker plus wg-quick on the local box, which the tunnel cannot carry
record.chaining: TCP only and purged monthly, so it serves a demo endpoint and not a WG peer.

limits.value: trial mappings cleared automatically after 30 days

record.binding_note: Monthly bandwidth allowance is 1 GB (approximately 0.0009 TiB) and port mappings expire after 30 days.

identity_cost.detail: The vendor sells from a mainland company address and answers support over QQ and WeChat, both of which are phone-bound.

record.reliability_note: Trial mappings are deleted after 30 days, and the vendor's own matrix marks the trial tier as having no SLA and no rapid failover.
record.confidence_note: The plan table was read out of the page HTML after the text extractor returned navigation only. The identity gate is unverified.

evidence.proved: trial edition is 0 yuan/year, 1 Mbps, 2 routes, 1 G/month, TCP and HTTP only, cleared after 30 days

record.notes: The price table is script-built: the reader returned navigation chrome and the numbers came from the raw HTML, which is why the protocol row is quotable at all. No UDP on the trial tier; whether a paid tier adds UDP is not stated on the page read.

extras.wg_detail: The trial edition's protocol row lists TCP and HTTP only. A 45 KB read of the pricing page contains no occurrence of UDP, and the native-port mapping the help centre describes is a TCP forward.
extras.volume_stated: 1 GB per month on the trial edition.
extras.transit_note: Vendor relays on multi-carrier domestic lines carry the tunnel.
